contract: Applications opt into terminal escape encoding. Requested event reporting distinguishes repeat and release; text-generating keys additionally require all-keys reporting.
Domicile_boundary: Application-to-terminal encoding and native Wayland keyboard delivery are separate layers.

contract: Main and alternate screens retain separate keyboard-mode stacks; push and pop operations restore the previous encoding state.
Domicile_boundary: This is terminal screen-mode state; desktop focus and window policy occupy other layers.

contract: With a positive repeat_info rate, repeatable key presses arm the client timer. Tracked release and focus loss stop it; delivery checks focus and a nonzero rate.
Domicile_boundary: Held-key repeat scheduling is separate from initial keypress delivery and display timing.

contract: Applications transmit raster data to the terminal. When emitted for an identified transmission, the reply reports pixel-data loading success or failure; quiet controls can suppress replies.
Domicile_boundary: The loading reply concerns terminal image data; it supplies no compositor presentation timestamp.

contract: The query action attempts image loading without storing or replacing an image. Its loading-status reply is subject to quiet controls.
Domicile_boundary: A terminal loading query and visible desktop presentation expose different observers.

contract: A placement displays retained image data. Emitted replies report image availability; quiet controls can suppress replies. Reusing an image and placement identifier pair replaces that placement.
Domicile_boundary: Placement acknowledgment and compositor presentation are separate contracts.

contract: The graphics protocol copies rectangular regions between frames of one image. Same-frame overlapping rectangles are rejected; expanding compact frame storage can return ENOSPC.
Domicile_boundary: This operates on terminal image frames; it establishes no Wayland capture export or compositor scene reconstruction.

contract: OSC5522 requests MIME types or data, reports denied access or unavailable selections, and can address PRIMARY separately from the clipboard.
Domicile_boundary: Terminal byte exchange and native Wayland selection resources are separate interfaces.

contract: When paste-event mode is enabled, a user-triggered paste announces available MIME types. The terminal application requests the desired data type.
Domicile_boundary: This is application-to-terminal negotiation; it establishes no particular application’s participation or Domicile clipboard format handling.

contract: Kitty provides DCS commands and an optional UNIX/TCP socket. Remote control defaults to disabled, with no configured listening socket.
Domicile_boundary: This controls the terminal process separately from the desktop window-control surface.

contract: A Wayland hold-begin event cancels Kitty’s local pointer momentum.
Domicile_boundary: Client momentum policy and compositor gesture transport remain separate.

contract: The client registry binds a seat only while no seat is stored.
Domicile_boundary: Multiple advertised server seats do not establish multiple independent participants in this client.

contract: input_delay postpones processing program output; repaint_delay controls screen-update spacing, with a bypass when input awaits processing.
Domicile_boundary: These are terminal scheduling controls; no effective Domicile render cadence follows from their definitions.

contract: The frame-ready handler records local monotonic time, marks rendering ready and schedules a tick. GLFW ignores the protocol timestamp; its helper can invoke readiness immediately while a swap awaits commit.
Domicile_boundary: Local readiness can follow a protocol callback or the immediate helper branch; it is not a visible-pixel timestamp.

contract: The default throughput benchmark suppresses screen rendering. Enabling rendering retains asynchronous rendering and batching effects.
Domicile_boundary: Parser throughput and terminal or desktop presentation timing are different observers.
